title: Add the durable file-set transaction kernel
description:
A reusable storage kernel prepares, publishes, rolls back, and completes one journaled set of file, mode, and directory actions under a caller-held guard, using an external bootstrap control plane when `.jit/` did not exist and `.jit/tmp/` otherwise.

## Background

The kernel implements the approved recoverable-publication contract for both existing repositories and fresh roots. It provides storage mechanics only; no existing writer or command adopts it in this leaf.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Prepared/committed/rolled-back decisions, rename-aside replacement, verified no-replace creation, synchronization, and typed recovery-required state implement the approved contract; a fresh-root rollback removes `.jit/` while its synchronized sibling journal remains, then records terminal rollback before cleanup.
- [hard] REQ-02: All production traversal/publication uses held `cap_std::fs::Dir` parents and capability-relative no-follow operations, with no `std::fs` pathname fallback; unsupported capability/filesystem behavior fails preflight, and created directories are handle-confined, parent-synced, and rollback-safe on Unix and Windows.
- [hard] REQ-03: Failure and race injection covers external/internal journal creation, every stage/sync/action/decision/reverse action, before/after fresh-root removal, terminal-residue cleanup, parent symlink/junction swap, cross-volume, mode, unexpected bootstrap occupant, and unexpected target occupant.

## Scope

**Blast radius:** new journal/staging/action/recovery-state modules plus narrowly reused artifact/atomic primitives, storage errors, and kernel failure tests; no existing writer or command changes yet.

**Green landing:** A caller-held-guard harness proves deterministic publication, exact handled rollback to both an existing repository and no `.jit/`, and resumable prepared/committed/rolled-back state without changing an existing writer or command.
